title: Profit on a life-saving drug
news: Intermediaries add an average 170% mark-up on cancer drugs; the government has capped the seller's profit at 30% of the MRP.
syllabus: Ethics in business and medicine · Compassion towards the weaker sections
link: When profit on life-saving medicines pushes patients to skip doses, business ethics demands that access to treatment come before margins.
question: "Life-saving medicines are a matter of right, not a market commodity." Examine the ethical issues in drug pricing.

title: Punishment and pendency: Need for, role of a sentencing council
syllabus: GS2 › Structure, organisation and functioning of the judiciary; Fundamental rights (Art 14, 21) · GS4 › Objectivity and impartiality
summary: Two legal experts argue that India's sentences depend on the judge, not the law, and propose a statutory Sentencing Council with guidelines and a national database, as in England.
evolution: Law Commission's 47th Report flags inconsistent sentencing (over 50 years ago).
Soman v State of Kerala: the SC calls sentencing one of the weakest parts of criminal justice.
Sunita Devi v State of Bihar: 'sentencing shall not be a mere lottery'; Centre told to examine a national sentencing policy, perhaps via a Sentencing Commission.
The Law Commission is examining the issue; recommendations expected soon.
ideas: Same crime, different sentence: punishment depends on the judge or Bench, not the law, because statutes give only maximums and minimums.
In India, two people convicted of the same crime can get very different sentences, depending more on the judge than the law.
Unguided discretion violates equality: arbitrary disparity offends Articles 14 and 21; research shows sentences cut for irrelevant factors such as a victim's 'chastity'.
Unguided sentencing discretion produces arbitrary disparity that is hard to square with Articles 14 and 21.
Probation and alternatives to prison exist in law (BNSS Sections 401–402; Probation of Offenders Act, 1958) but are rarely used without a framework.
Alternatives to custody exist under the BNSS and the Probation of Offenders Act, but without guidance courts seldom use them.
Appeals burden: higher courts correct sentences case by case, without a common yardstick, adding to pendency.
Without sentencing guidelines, appellate courts spend scarce time correcting harsh or lenient sentences case by case.

A Sentencing Council by law: offence-wise guidelines (seriousness, starting point, individualisation), a national database on the NJDG, and guidelines placed before Parliament, presumptive but not binding.
A statutory Sentencing Council, as in England, can make judicial discretion accountable without ending judicial independence.

title: Ageing with dignity
news: After its elder-rights law, Keralam is urged to build a silver economy without weakening welfare.
syllabus: Compassion towards the weaker sections · Role of family and society in inculcating values
link: Respect and care for the old, and their right to choose how they participate, is a test of a society's values.
question: Is 'productive ageing' an opportunity for the elderly or a way to shift the state's responsibility onto them? Discuss ethically.

title: Sentencing and objectivity
news: Two experts show that similar offenders get very different sentences depending on the judge, and propose a Sentencing Council.
link: Objectivity means like cases treated alike, on law and evidence, not personal views; guidelines make discretion accountable.
question: Discretion is essential in administration, yet it can become arbitrary. How can objectivity be ensured in discretionary decisions? Illustrate with an example.

title: Keralam makes elder care a right
news: Keralam passed India's first state law giving senior citizens enforceable rights to care and dignity.
syllabus: Empathy, tolerance and compassion towards the weaker sections
link: Dignity in old age moves from charity to entitlement; the state supports the family's duty rather than replacing it.
question: Is care of the elderly a family duty or a responsibility of the state? Discuss in the light of dignity and compassion.

title: Cyclone Arnab: the most vulnerable first
news: Andhra Pradesh moved 4,711 pregnant women to hospitals before the cyclone; Odisha sent ministers to the districts.
syllabus: Compassion towards the weaker sections · Accountability and ethical governance
link: The care ethics of the state, and a best practice in disaster management: plan for those who cannot protect themselves.
question: 'The ethics of care is the first principle of disaster management.' Discuss with an example.
